title: One wave orchestrator oversees every lane on events: heartbeats, deadlines, quota walls, landings and the measures
summary: No component oversees all lanes of a wave together. The console does it by hand with `wave watch`, `wave status` and the merge steps at the boundary. Practice: a pre-dispatch overlap check and a maximum independent set of non-conflicting work, and a merge queue with speculative checks (Mergify, Uber SubmitQueue).
fix: Plan components O6 (D10, D11, D12) and O7 (D14), spec sections 9 and 11. One goroutine in the loop reads the ADR-0127 channels cycle, ship, errors and loop through internal/events/reader and never polls. It frees cells on ship.landed, re-sizes on a clihealth bench, and reports stalls. It does not predict conflicts (research P3.7) and does not land (ADR-0128, ADR-0134). Design: docs/plans/wave-orchestrator-2026-10.md and docs/architecture/wave-orchestrator.md (ADR-0139).
acceptance: `TestOrchestrator_WakesOnlyOnEvents` and `TestOrchestrator_ShipLandedFreesTheCells` pass, and the ADR-0127 AST guard bans poll timers in the package.
`TestWaveStatus_ReportsTheConflictRate` passes: `evolve wave status --json` reports width_sized, width_realized, utilization, supply, admission_waits, conflict_rate and deadline_stops.
